description_text:
CURATED STREET, ENVIRONMENT & CHARACTERS PARK MEGA PACK (128 PREMIUM 3D MODELS)
Expand your miniature worlds and architectural layouts with the most comprehensive outdoor and character asset library available. Natively modeled and optimized at a 1:50 scale, this Street, Environment & Characters Park Mega Pack features 128 unique premium objects meticulously engineered for flawless FDM and Resin (SLA) printing.
This specialized collection brings your scenery to life by combining urban infrastructure, outdoor furniture, low-poly vehicles, and a diverse set of detailed human scale figures.
IMPORTANT: OUTDOOR ENVIRONMENT & CHARACTERS ONLY (LIMITED EDITION)Please note: This specific package contains OUTDOOR ASSETS, VEHICLES, AND HUMAN FIGURES ONLY. It DOES NOT INCLUDE any indoor home furniture or interior appliances. 
Want the absolute full library with no restrictions? If you need both the entire interior collection PLUS all outdoor street, landscape environment, and character props, please visit our store profile page and check out our flagship Ultimate Pack (454 models total)!
WHAT’S INSIDE THIS MEGA PACK?You will receive 128 unique high-fidelity models, cleanly organized into distinct categories across 3 universal formats: .STL, .OBJ, and .3MF.

  - STREET (WITH SUPPORTS) — 52 itemsIntricate environmental structures, detailed trees, deciduous and evergreen plants, rocks, and complex terrain assets requiring support coordination.

  - STREET (SUPPORT-FREE) — 49 itemsNegligible bridging props engineered to print flat on the bed with 0 supports needed: modular benches, picnic tables, fences, gates, bus stops, pergolas, and outdoor sports equipment.

  - PEOPLE & CHARACTERS — 25 itemsHighly detailed 3D human figures in realistic casual, walking, sitting, and standing poses. Essential for showcasing true architectural scale and adding life to dioramas.

  - LOW-POLY VEHICLES — 2 itemsArchitectural scale background vehicles (Hatchback car and a Pickup truck) to enrich your street layouts. Also includes scale silhouettes.

BONUS: Interactive Premium Preview Book Included (PDF)Stop searching blindly through hundreds of raw files! Your download includes a beautifully formatted, magazine-style Interactive PDF Catalog to browse your outdoor and character assets on your PC or smartphone:

  - Smart Table of Contents: Clean page numbering with automated item counters for fluid navigation.

  - Visual Chapter Covers: Premium pre-rendered layout overviews for every category.

  - 2x4 Layout Sheets: Large, crisp dual-angle renders for all 128 models.

  - Technical Dimensions: Real-world measurements printed right beneath the model names.

  - Support Complexity Indicators: Integrated * and ** markings warning you instantly if a specific model needs minimal slicer supports or advanced handling.

EXCLUSIVE FEATURE: Combined Master ScenesTime is money. For professional architects, landscape designers, and kitbashers, we have included Combined Master Scenes for each category in .OBJ and .STL. Instead of dragging and dropping individual files, you can load an entire asset group into your favorite software (Blender, 3ds Max, Rhino, AutoCAD) or your slicer in just one single click!
SLICER SCALE CHEAT SHEETThe models are native to a 1:50 scale. To adapt the library to your specific project needs, simply check Uniform Scaling (lock aspect ratio for X, Y, Z axes) in your slicer (Cura, PrusaSlicer, Bambu Studio, Chitubox) and input the following percentages:

  - 1:12 Scale  Set to 416.7% (Large diorama/collector setups)

  - 1:25 Scale  Set to 200.0% (Double the original size)

  - 1:50 Scale  Set to 100.0% (Original native design scale)

  - 1:75 Scale  Set to 66.67% (Mid-size layout projects)

  - 1:100 Scale  Set to 50.0% (Exactly half the size)

  - 1:150 Scale  Set to 33.33% (Micro-architectural modeling)

  - 1:200 Scale  Set to 25.0% (Ultra-miniature engineering layouts)

MICRO-SCALING WARNING: When downscaling models to ultra-small sizes (1:100 down to 1:200), fine features like thin branches, fence grids, vehicle mirrors, or character limbs become microscopic. For flawless results at small scales, a well-calibrated SLA (Resin) printer or a specialized 0.2mm FDM nozzle is highly recommended.
TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS & LICENSING

  - File Formats: .STL, .OBJ, .3MF (Clean manifold geometry, high compatibility).

  - Print-Tested: Every asset has been physically printed, refined, and verified by the author. No corrupted shells or un-sliceable open edges.

  - Delivery: Instant Digital Download. You will receive a text file with a direct, secure Google Drive link right after purchase.

Note: This listing contains digital files for 3D printing only. No physical plastic parts will be shipped.

description_text:
A boat trailer is a trailer designed to launch, retrieve, carry and sometimes store boats. Commercial hydraulic boat trailers are used by marinas, boat yards, boat haulers, boat dealers and boat builders. Generally this type of trailer is not used for storage of the boat.
Self-propelledSelf-propelled boat movers are not trailers in the strictest sense of the word. They are hydraulically operated boat movers, with their own tractor unit. They share all of the features of hydraulic boat trailers.This type of trailer is usually used by the boat owner/operator. The trailer is also used for storage.
Roll-on, also known as a Roller style trailer, uses rubber and/or polyurethane rollers for ease of launching and loading a boat.Glide-path, also known as a Float-on style trailer, allows the boat to float onto the trailer; after the trailer has been partially submerged (usually 3⁄4 of the trailer). Since its inception, it has become quite popular compared to the Roller style trailer.

description_text:
Intended for 3d print.UPDATE 20230122: Added four-way crossing. See image gallery.
Simple 3d-printable, modular railroad grid. Compatible with most tabletop miniature games.
This kit includes 6 model parts (7 if you count the separate buffer stop), allowing you to build a railroad grid that can be extended indefinitely. All railroad sections fit together without any modification needed (imagine every section as either one square, or multiple squares, in a square grid). As long as the railroad is contiguous, it is guaranteed fit together at any and all junctions.
The default scale of the kit is roughly 28mm. However, all model parts should function without problem at virtually any commonly used scale you want to print them at. Please note that the railroad grid may be too thin at sub-6mm scale.
A few notes on design
I've put some effort into making the railroad models faithful to real railroad tracks. But this is still mainly intended to be a generic railroad grid useable in many various games and settings. If you are looking for highly realistic miniature tracks, this model kit might not be for you. 
Also note that the model sections with rails crossing or merging do not contain any switches. For various reasons, adding junctions and crossings with detailed switches would be too time consuming. Instead I've simply combined curves and/or straight sections to create junctions. The result is fairly unsophisticated, so I recommend looking closely at the junctions and crossing sections in the image gallery before purchasing. Again, this is not a product in which realism is the main priority.
Detailed model parts list

  - 1 Straight Section

  - 1 Small Curve

  - 1 Big Curve

  - 1  Curve and Straight Junction

  - 1 Two Curves Junction

  - 1 Buffer Stop

  - 1 Buffer Stop separated from track

  - 1 Crossing (added 20230122)

description_text:
Worm gear collection modeled in Inventor 2010 and provided in multiple file formats (.IPT, .STP, .STL, .3DS, .OBJ). Collection includes 3 worm gear sizes (16-tooth, 24-tooth, and 32-tooth), 3 spur gear sizes (16-tooth, 24-tooth, and 32-tooth), and 2 worm styles (compatible with spur gears and compatible with worm gears), all fully ready for 3D printing.
The native Inventor files are fully parametric and can be opened and manipulated in any version of the software that is 2010 or newer. The feature trees and parameter tables are logically arranged and clearly labeled, making edits extremely simple.
All gears have been exported as STP files, allowing them to be opened in any 3D CAD software. They have also been exported as 3DS and OBJ files, for use in 3D graphics packages. Finally, they are provided as STL files, making them ready for 3D printing.
Strategic recesses have been engineered into the larger gears to minimize their volume for the purpose of reducing the cost of 3D printing.
Worm / spur gear set fully compatible with Spur Gear Collection 02.
No textures or materials included.
Gear specifications:

  - Approximate involute gear tooth profile

  - Minimal backlash between gears

  - 1/4 inch face width

  - 1/4 inch shaft bore

  - 16 Pitch (P) gear size

  - Pitch Diameter (PD) = Gear Teeth (T) / Pitch (P)

  - Outside Diameter (OD) = Pitch Diameter (PD) + 0.125 inch

  - Worms provided with bore for 1/4 inch ANSI D-profile shaft

  - Worm gears and spur gears provided with bore for 1/4 inch round shaft with standard ANSI 3/32 inch keyway

  - Polygon counts range from 22,016 (16-tooth spur gear) to 56,866 (32-tooth worm gear)

Product includes:

  - Worm gear set Inventor 2010 files (IPT)

  - Worm gear set STP files (for other 3D CAD packages)

  - Worm gear set STL files (for 3D printing)

  - Worm gear set 3DS files (for 3D graphics packages)

  - Worm gear set OBJ files (for 3D graphics packages)

  - Sample worm gear animation (AVI)

description_text:
Universal joint, fully functional, accurately modeled, and ready for use in CAD, CGI, and 3D print applications. Modeled in Autodesk Inventor and provided in multiple file formats. Perfect for both digital and physical mechanical design projects.
Universal joints are used to couple two rotating shafts that are not parallel. They are commonly used with automobile drive shafts, steering columns, and a variety of industrial equipment.
Universal joint specifications:

  - Shaft diameter: 1.000in

  - Outside diameter: 1.500in

  - Overall length: 4.000in

  - Maximum operarting angle: 30.0deg

3 Provisions are included to mount the universal joint to your shafts:

  - Keyway cut into bore

  - Thru hole for spring pins

  - Pilot hole that can be drilled and tapped to accept set screws

Universal joint is sized for a 1.000in diameter shaft. But parts can be easily scaled to use with any shaft diameter of your choice, in imperial or metric dimensions.
Scaling factors for common shaft sizes:

  - 1.000in shaft = 100% scale

  - 0.750in shaft = 75% scale

  - 0.500in shaft = 50% scale

  - 0.250in shaft = 25% scale

  - 25mm shaft = 98.43% scale

  - 20mm shaft = 78.74% scale

  - 15mm shaft = 59.06% scale

  - 10mm shaft = 39.37% scale

Native Autodesk Inventor 2012 files are provided with intact browser trees and parameter tables to allow full configurability and customization.
Product includes:

  - 3 Autodesk Inventor 2012 part files for CAD (IPT format) - includes fork, block, and pin

  - 2 Autodesk Inventor 2012 assembly files for CAD (IAM format) - includes finished assembly and exploded assembly

  - 1 Autodesk Inventor 2012 drawing file for CAD (IDW format)

  - 5 STP models for CAD - includes finished assembly, exploded assembly, fork, block, and pin

  - 5 SAT models for CAD - includes finished assembly, exploded assembly, fork, block, and pin

  - 5 IGS models for CAD - includes finished assembly, exploded assembly, fork, block, and pin

  - 3 STL models for 3D print - fork, block, and pin

  - 1 OBJ model for CGI - includes finished assembly

  - 1 3DS model for CGI - includes finished assembly

  - 1 FBX model for CGI - includes finished assembly

  - 2 Viewable, read-only 3d models (DWF format, open using Autodesk Design Review free download) - includes finished assembly and exploded assembly

  - 1 Detail drawing (DWG format)

  - 1 Detail drawing (PDF format)

  - 1 Read Me text file (TXT format) detailing the physical dimensions and quantities of all parts required to build the assembly

If you have any questions, either before or after purchasing this model, please feel free to contact me here on CGTrader and I will help in any way possible.

description_text: Knuckle joint is an important mechanical joint used in structures to connect two cylindrical rods if their axes lie in the same plane. Knuckle joint provides angular movement between cylindrical rods and it is specially designed to withstand tensile loads. Knuckle joint is named so because it can rotate freely on axis of knuckle pin.               Knuckle joint has following parts:               1) Knuckle fork              2) Knuckle pin               3) Eye end rod               4) Taper pin               5) CollarAll the above parts are visualized in the exploded view image of knuckle joint. Advantages : 1) It can withstand high tensile loads                           2) It has good mechanical rigidity                            3) It is easy to manufacture and setup                          4) Design is simple and easy. Applications : They are used in                              1) Bicycle chains                             2) Tractors, trusses                             3) Automobile Wipers                           4) Cranes , Earth Movers                            5) Robotic Joints                           6) Structural Members

description_text:
Sci-fi Desert Dino speeder / spaceship / flyer model. Made in 3dsMax2022 and textured in Substance Painter. Renders were created in SP Iray renderer. Model has 11592 polygons and 11238 vertices.
Model details:

  - Model pack contains .fbx / .max / .blend and .obj file formats. Textures aren’t embedded into each format and have to be plugged in manually. 

  - Fbx files are provided for 2014/2015, 2016/2017 and 2020 versions.

  - You might want to rescale the model to match scene size

  - Side pipes, engine connectors, turbine engine shafts and nozzles share same texture set (overlapping UVs)

  - Model is centered to the middle of its bottom part and placed to 0.0.0 scene coordinates

  - Textures come in a single 4k UV set

  - Texture pack contains .png textures optimized for Arnold, Vray, Corona, UnityHDmetal + .png/.jpeg and .targa files optimized for UE4

  - Nothing is animated

  - UV maps can be seen in screenshots section

  - Everything is named properly

  - Engines have their emissive map and a common metal map (when they are shut down)

Make sure to contact me if you want more details or some minor adaptations to the model.
As usual: best wishes and have a nice day!:D

description_text:
Intended for 3D print.
Mobile tower. Suitable for steampunk settings, or as towers for certain weird psychic greenskins in a certain grimdark tabletop game.
Intended to be used as a main gun alternative for the Ork Panzer Buggy kit (link below). But can be used with other 28mm vehicles, or as a standalone model, with some conversion work.
Please note that the Mobile Tower kit only contains the actual tower. The Panzer Buggy depicted in certain images are only included to provide context. The red colouration indicates which sections are part of the kit.
The individual parts of this model are packed in a .rar archive containing a number of .stl files. Each .stl file contains a part of the model, or one of several different variations of the model. See the bulletpoint list below for a detailed description of the model parts included in the kit.
Model Parts

  - Mobile Tower Housing

  - Mobile Tower Housing With Widow's Walk (a circular platform you can place additional miniatures on).

  - Leaning Mobile Tower Housing (a slightly tilted variant to give your tower a slightly rickety feel).

  - Mobile Tower With Solid Interiors (a variant of the tower with no hollow interiors. To be used if. for example, you want to print the tower in a smaller scale where the walls would otherwise become too thin to print).

  - Mobile tower With Widow's Walk and Solid Interiors (same as above).

  - Mobile Tower Roofs (Two different versions, one with smoke coming out of the chimney and one without).

  - Mobile Tower Parts (contains a number of accessories for the tower, including windows that can be opened or closed, a door than can be opened or closed, a large and small satellite dish, two ravens and an orky window ornament).

For more news and information from Sharedog Miniatures, follow me on Instagram under the handle #sharedogminiatures.

description_text:
Intended for 3d print.
UPDATE 20250923: Model has a sealed internal void in the cargo compartment section of the model. This void isn't really an issue for printing, but nonetheless I've added a version with this void removed. 
UPDATE 20220919: I cut the Ordinatus model into 4 parts roughly equal in size (original, uncut model still included).Use these parts if your printer area is insufficient to house the original model in its entirety. Please note that I didn't put any great effort into cutting the model up. Imagine a giant cake slicer cutting vertically straight through the original model...I also added presupported versions of all model parts included in the product.
Heavy-duty truck carrying a gigantic plasma cannon. Suitable for tabletop games in the scales between 6mm and 28mm. Note that some of the finer details will not show up at smaller scales.
This is a modified version of the Modular Superheavy Tank model kit (see link below). Note that the Extra-Ordinatus and Modular Tank kits are not compatible. You cannot use model parts from the Modular Superheavy Tank with the Extra-Ordinatus, or vice versa.  
The Extra-Ordinatus kit contains the following model parts:

  - 1 Extra-Ordinatus Mobile Megacannon Tolered (Note: entire vehicle prints as one part. At default scale, this requires a print bed with dimensions of approximately 18x12x10cm. It can be reduced in size to about 80 percent of default scale, and still work for 28mm scale. )

  - 1 Sandbag wall

  - 1 Floodlight

description_text:
Intended for 3d print.
PLEASE NOTE: This product only includes Landmaster Tri-Star wheels. The tank body depicted in certain images is there for contextual purposes only, and is NOT included in this product.
Tri-star wheel arrangement. The concept was originated by Robert and John Forsyth, of Lockheed, in 1967. It is most known for having been used by the Landmaster vehicles in the 1977 post-apocalyptic movie Damnation Alley. The main advantage of the design is that if one wheel gets stuck on an obstacle, the next wheel will rotate over it and thus clear the obstacle. I am unsure of its applicability in real life, but in Make-Belief Land the tri-star wheels are suitable for rough terrain (and for running over radscorpions...).The Landmaster Tri-star kit is mainly intended to be used with the Modular Superheavy Tank by Sharedog Miniatures (sold separately, see link below). Most of the wheel models have been specifically adjusted to make them compatible with the Modular Superheavy Tank. But there is also set of tri-star wheels included that is suitable for use with vehicles from other tabletop miniatures manufacturers. See detailed list below.
Detailed list
This product includes a number of different tri-star versions. 

  - A set of normal proportioned wheels (divided into left, right, front and rear models).

  - A set of oversized wheels (divided into left and right models).

  - Another set of oversized wheels, but with the protective rail removed from much of the models.

  - A set of wheels (divided into left and right models) that are not intended to be used with the Modular Superheavy Tank, but instead as alternative propulsion for tabletop vehicles in general. Whereas the wheel models intended for use with the Modular Superheavy Tank have uneven inward-facing surfaces (see images) that might make them difficult to use with other vehicles, the inward facing surfaces of the non-specific wheels are flat and relatively easy to kitbash with any type of vehicle.

  - Finally, the Landmaster Tri-star kit also includes a dozer blade, and a Landmaster name sign used in Damnation Alley.

Assembly
You will have to print a minimum of 4 models to make a full set of ordinary size wheels. You will have to print a minimum of 2 models for a full set of oversized wheels. Mounting the wheels onto the Modular Superheavy Tank is relatively easy - just push the wheels horizontally onto the main tank body, inserting the studs of the main tank body into the corresponding holes on the tri-star wheel models. See image gallery for further information. Note that glue will likely be required to hold the model parts together. 
Recommended Scale
The tri-star wheels are primarily intended for use in 28mm scale tabletop games, but will likely work for any scale down to and including 20mm scale. The wheels are primarily intended to be used as alternative propulsion for the Modular Superheavy Tank kit made by Sharedog Miniatures, sold separately. Link below. All model parts in the Landmaster Tri-Star Wheels kit have been prescaled to fit the default scale of the Modular Superheavy Tank. As long as you alter neither model size-wise, they should fit together. But always check the size of all models prior to printing to make sure. The wheels are also reasonably compatible with tanks from other miniatures manufacturers.

description_text: The Pa 100 Flying Arrow, designed by Nicolas-Roland Payen was expected to attend the Coupe Deutsch of Meurthe 1933. Derived Project K 16 (SP.260 model with retractable train) and K 16 B (model RP. 261 fixed train), the unit was equipped with a delta wing (a term assigned in the years 1948, comes from the similarity of this form with the 4th letter of the Greek alphabet), a fixed train, plans before equipped with shutters to ensure the stability at low speeds (those little wings called machutes will later named canard), the expected engine was a Regnier six inverted cylinder 180 hp with a two-bladed propeller. (Source : http://jn.passieux.free.fr/html/Pa100.php)

description_text: The North American Aviation T-6 Texan was a single-engined advanced trainer aircraft used to train pilots of the United States Army Air Forces (USAAF), United States Navy, Royal Air Force and other air forces of the British Commonwealth during World War II and into the 1970s. Designed by North American Aviation, the T-6 is known by a variety of designations depending on the model and operating air force. The United States Army Air Corps (USAAC) and USAAF designated it as the AT-6, the United States Navy the SNJ, and British Commonwealth air forces, the Harvard, the name it is best known by outside of the US. After 1962, US forces designated it the T-6. It remains a popular warbird aircraft used for airshow demonstrations and static displays. It has also been used many times to simulate the Japanese Mitsubishi Zero in movies depicting World War II in the Pacific. (Source Wikipedia)

description_text:
A windlass is a machine used on ships that is used to let-out and heave-up equipment such as a ship's anchor or a fishing trawl. On some ships, it may be located in a specific room called the windlass room.
An anchor windlass is a machine that restrains and manipulates the anchor chain on a boat, allowing the anchor to be raised and lowered by means of chain cable. A notched wheel engages the links of the chain or the rope.
A trawl windlass is a similar machine that restrains or manipulates the trawl on a commercial fishing vessel. The trawl is a sort of big fishing net that is wound on the windlass. The fishermen either let-out the trawl or heave-up the trawl during fishing operations. A brake is provided for additional control. The windlass is usually powered by an electric or hydraulic motor operating via a gear train.

description_text:
Fully printable - no support - no glue - single color 3D printer
This is a city bus toy (short version, you can also find a long version/with an (TPU)articulation in my library...)
It is completely 3d printable.The tolerance for pieces that need to fit tightly is 0.1mm,for pieces that need to allow movement (like screws and axles) 0.3mm.
Assemble video-tutorial  https://youtu.be/IdtFxOJIjbE
Printing list:  Nb. STL file name                     rezolution  support     colour

  -  2x axle_die.stl                      0.16mm      no          gray

  - 1x back_face.stl                     0.12mm      no          red/blue/black

  - either:**  1x base_front_back.stl             0.16mm      no          gray**  1x base_front_front.stl            0.16mm      no          gray
or**  1x base_front_full.stl             0.16mm      no          gray

  - either:**  1x body_front_back.stl             0.16mm      no          white/blue**  1x body_front_front.stl            0.16mm      no          white/blue
or**  1x body_front_full.stl             0.16mm      no          white/blue

  - 1x front_face.stl                    0.12mm      no          blue/white/blue

  - 1x front_number_cap.stl              0.12mm      no          blue

  - 2x rim_double.stl                    0.12mm      yes(plate)  white         

  - 2x rim_single.stl                    0.12mm      yes(plate)  white          

  - 2x screw_9mm.stl                     0.16mm      no          red         

  - 3x screw_9mm.stl                     0.16mm      no          gray    

  - 0x sleeping_screw_9mm.stl            0.16mm      no

  - 8x screw_13mm.stl                    0.16mm      no          orange    

  - 0x sleeping_screw_13mm.stl           0.16mm      no

  - 2x screw_double_wheel.stl            0.12mm      no          blue       

  - 2x screw_front_wheel.stl             0.12mm      no          white      

  - 1x sliding_doors.stl                 0.12mm      no          orange

  - 1x steering_wheel.stl                0.12mm      no          black        

  - 2x tire_bus_simple.stl               0.16mm      no          black (TPU) 

  - 4x tire_bus_with_outter_cut.stl      0.16mm      no          black (TPU)

The front face, back face and body where printed with changing the materials for a multi-colour effect:

To print the shell, do not fill the whole shell with support material. Just place three or four supports over the length of the shell. Also the windows in the shell can be printed without supports. It worked perfectly on my cr10. description_text:
screw_ladder_base_sleeping_v1.stlFully printable - no glue - single color 3D printer
Fire truck toy I designed and printed for my son.
Print with a machine that handles tolerances of 0.3-0.4 mm, if it doesn't, things won't fit together, and the ladder peaces will most probably stick to each other. Print the screws and dies with a layer not thicker than 0.16mm (did not try a coarser one, so no guaranty that it will work...), I recommend 0.12mm.Print list: quantity - stl file name - used collor - position for printing - observation:

  - 2x - die_connection_69p6mm_r6p7.stl - blue - as it is - no support

  - 1x - front_grill.stl - black - turn 90 deg over Y - no support

  - 1x - back_top.stl - yellow - as it is - no support

  - 1x - back_grill_lights.stl - red - turn 90 deg over Y - no support

  - 1x - ladder_base.stl - red - as it is - with support

  - 1x - ladder_in_out.stl - white - upside down - with support

  - 1x - cockpit.stl - black - as it is - with support

  - 1x - trunk_stairs.stl - red - turn 180 deg over Y - with support

  - 1x - cabin.stl - red - turn 90 deg over Y - with support

  - 1x - seats_2_rows.stl - black - as it is - no support

  - 1x - side_left.stl - white - turn 90 deg over X - no support

  - 1x - side_right.stl - white - turn 90 deg over X - no support

  - 2x - wheel_axle_100mm_r5p5.stl - black - as it is - no support

  - 3x - die_connection_69p6mm_r5p5.stl - blue - as it is - no support

  - 4x - screw_ladder_base.stl - yellow - as it is - no support

  - 6x - screw_20mm_filet_10mm_full.stl - yellow -  as it is - no support

  - 4x - screw_20mm_filet_10mm_full.stl - white - as it is - no support

  - 4x - screw_27mm_filet.stl - black - as it is - no support

  - 2x - fire_truck_roof_light.stl - blue - as it is - no support

  - 2x - roof_light_LEFT_HAND.stl - blue - as it is - no support

  - 1x - fire_truck_roof_light.stl - red - as it is - no support

  - 1x - roof_light_LEFT_HAND.stl - red -  as it is - no support

  - 2x - fire_truck_roof_light.stl - white - as it is - no support

  - 2x - wheel_left.stl - black - as it is - with support

  - 2x - wheel_right.stl - black - as it is - with support

  - 4x - wheel_cap.stl - white - as it is - no support

  - 1x - lader_axle_72mm_r5p5.stl  - white - as it is - no support

  - 2x - front_light.stl - blue - turn 90 deg over Y - no support

For the assembly steps check the photos. 
Hopefully I did not miss any stl files, if I did, leave a comment.
Some adjustments to the long/big parts such that the model can be printed on smaller beds (20x20cm).

  - I splited the side parts in two and connected them with two small screws.

  - Therefore do not print:
  - 1x - side_left.stl - white - turn 90 deg over X  - no support

  - 1x - side_right.stl  - white - turn 90 deg over X - no support

  - But print these instead:
  - 4x - screw_small_l12mm.stl - any - as it is - no support

  - 1x - side_left_back.stl  - white - turn 90 deg over X - with support

  - 1x - side_left_front.stl - white -  turn 90 deg over X -  no support

  - 1x - side_right_back.stl - white - turn 90 deg over X  with support

  - 1x - side_right_front.stl - white -  turn 90 deg over X - no support

  - I cut the ladder to be shorter (220mm) such that it can be printed on a 20x20cm bed diagonal.

  - Therefore do not print:  - 1x - ladder_in_out.stl - white - upside down - with support

  - But print these instead:  - 1X - ladder_short_220mm.stl  - white - upside down - with support

The model was initially posted on https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3457842
I will be posting soon my new platform for a truck toy...
The model was designed with Freecad, I can therefor also upload the Freecad project file with it...
Update 04.2021:Because the axles and/or axle screws and the ladder base screws are breaking often (if also printed with PLA) I redesigned them similar to the other truck models. For this use this:

  - axle_l100mm_new.stl instead of the original axle

  - cap_double_rim.stl instead of the original screws

  - screw_ladder_base_sleeping_v1.stl instead of the original lader base screws(prind directions as in the files)Check the last picture to understand what I mean.

I used Bambu slicer (Prusa slicer) organic tree supports included into a brim for the from cabin doors and the windshield cantilevered bridges, on my first print the author’s supports failed without the brim, but maybe with a brim they would have been just fine, that recommendation could have been very appreciated in the instructions. Overall the project took me about a week time in Bambu P1P , I took a lot of time to dial in settings learn from the failed prints etc. in the sheer print time the model on my p1p took about 45 hours of direct print time (failed prints included) it can be printed now faster NCR I am very familiar with the designs, 24+ hours I think on p1p. As for everything else and the impressions overall it can be felt how much love and ingenuity and time!!!! is put into the toy by the author, love the authors attention to detail and design - some improvement still possible here and there but I would definitely consider buying more designs and printing other toys. Thank you! Merci beaucoup ! Sincerely Your, SURF3DMORE INFORMATION ABOUT 3D MODELS :
THE CAMSHAFT IS A ROTATING OBJECT USUALLY MADE OF METAL  THAT CONTAINS POINTED CAMS, WHICH CONVERTS ROTATIONAL MOTION TO RECIPROCAL MOTION. CAMSHAFTS ARE USED IN INTERNAL COMBUSTION ENGINES (TO OPERATE THE INTAKE AND EXHAUST VALVES), MECHANICALLY CONTROLLED IGNITION SYSTEMS AND EARLY ELECTRIC MOTOR SPEED CONTROLLERS. CAMSHAFTS IN AUTOMOBILES ARE MADE FROM STEEL OR CAST IRON, AND ARE A KEY FACTOR IN DETERMINING THE RPM RANGE OF AN ENGINE'S POWER BAND.
IN PISTON ENGINES, THE CAMSHAFT IS USED TO OPERATE THE INTAKE AND EXHAUST VALVES. THE CAMSHAFT CONSISTS OF A CYLINDRICAL ROD RUNNING THE LENGTH OF THE CYLINDER BANK WITH A NUMBER OF CAMS (DISCS WITH PROTRUDING CAM LOBES) ALONG ITS LENGTH, ONE FOR EACH VALVE. A CAM LOBE FORCES A VALVE OPEN BY PRESSING ON THE VALVE, OR ON SOME INTERMEDIATE MECHANISM, AS IT ROTATES. MEANWHILE, A SPRING EXERTS A TENSION PULLING THE VALVE TOWARD ITS CLOSED POSITION. WHEN THE LOBE REACHES ITS HIGHEST DISPLACEMENT ON THE PUSH ROD, THE VALVE IS COMPLETELY OPEN. THE VALVE IS CLOSED WHEN THE SPRING PULLS IT BACK AND THE CAM IS ON ITS BASE CIRCLE.

A typical key is a small piece of metal consisting of two parts: the bit or blade, which slides into the keyway of the lock and distinguishes between different keys, and the bow, which is left protruding so that torque can be applied by the user. In its simplest implementation, a key operates one lock or set of locks that are keyed alike, a lock/key system where each similarly keyed lock requires the same, unique key. The key serves as a security token for access to the locked area; only persons having the correct key can open the lock and gain access. In more complex mechanical lock/key systems, two different keys, one of which is known as the master key, serve to open the lock. Common metals include brass, plated brass, nickel silver, and steel.

Upon purchase, you will get 3 files for each file format specified on the right column:

  - Tire 1, the least detailed of all. Simplified tread and blank sides with no letters inscribed.

description_text:
Extra Truck Chassis is a collection of 3D printable files that includes two new chassis, a tracked option, a trailer, and additional detail pieces that can be added to our truck kits for more variety. They have been designed to print easily and to work with 28-32mm scale figures. 
This is an EXPANSION KIT, and will require owning one of our other kits like the Military Truck, Halftrack Recovery, or Outpost Utility to use. The extra truck chassis are shown on the Military Truck and Halftrack Recovery kit below.
Printing
This is a kit, and requires assembly. The pieces are designed to be printed on a home FDM 3D printer with:

  - A 0.4mm nozzle.

  - 0.08 - 0.12 mm layer height.

  - 15 - 20% infill.

  - Supports are only required for a few of the .STL files.

  - Rafts may be required for the smaller parts, depending on your 3D printer.

  - The largest part is 102mm long, so this kit can be printed on a 110mm or larger build plate.

All .STL files are oriented correctly so you can load them into your slicer and print them immediately. The parts have been designed to print face-up for the best detail. All .STL files were sliced using Cura and test printed on a Creality Ender 3.

description_text:
This is for adding a 140mm disc brake to bikes without them.Its original intent was for adding front brakes to small electric kids motorcycles for better stopping power.Designed for the MX350 to use the MX650/RSF350 brake calipers or regular bike calipers with the appropriate adapter (without the cone washers).Of course you can use larger discs by using different adapters.
I am including instructions for uploading to SendCutSend for getting manufactured.
Dimensions:

  - Thickness: 3mm 

  - Axle hole: 10mm

  - Adjacent to axle hole: 4.2mm (M5 tap)

  - Fork fastener holes: 3x 5.1mm (M5 clearance)

I dont recommend braking while going in reverse as you are relying on the threads or rivets to not pull out of potentially thin-walled steel tube. This is strongest in the direction of the normal braking forces.You can also skip bolting and riveting by welding if it is made from mild-steel
Models:

  - .dxf of the mount for cutting and bending

  - .stl of the mount for mock-up

  - .stl of a version of the 160f/140r caliper adapter

  - .stl of a couple spacers

The info could also be changed to white if that is your thing. or really any other color for that matter.The materials of modern pneumatic tires are synthetic rubber, natural rubber, fabric and wire, along with carbon black and other chemical compounds. They consist of a tread and a body. The tread provides traction while the body provides containment for a quantity of compressed air. Before rubber was developed, the first versions of tires were simply bands of metal fitted around wooden wheels to prevent wear and tear. Early rubber tires were solid (not pneumatic). Pneumatic tires are used on many types of vehicles, including cars, bicycles, motorcycles, buses, trucks, heavy equipment, and aircraft. Metal tires are still used on locomotives and railcars, and solid rubber (or other polymer) tires are still used in various non-automotive applications, such as some casters, carts, lawnmowers, and wheelbarrows.

description_text:
Old truck converted to a movable gate with gunports. This terrain piece is created mainly for Orks (Warhammer40k) but can easily fit into other sci-fi games and settings.
This model is free for all my Patrons. You can support me & get the model for free at my Patreon.com/PrintaBoy
Key features:

  - 28mm scale

  - print is tested on FDM Ender 5 printer

  - dimensions of the completed print is 175 x 67 x 79 mm

  - the platform is designed to fit 10x25mm bases or 5x32mm bases

  - whole model consist of 6 separate pieces that need to be glued together.

  - all parts are rotated and positioned - STLs are plug & print ready

  - no supports needed

Assembly instructions:1) Print 2x FrontWheel, 2x RearWheelAxis and 4x RearWheel. Print the rest only once.2) Glue FrontWheel to FrontWheelAxis3) Glue RearWheel to RearWheelAxis (repeat for second pair of wheels and axis)4) Glue parts 2) and 3) to the slots on the bottom of OrkGate5) Glue Engine to the slot on OrkGate
You can skip points 2) to 4) if you don't want wheels on the gate.
3D Printing Settings
Infill: 15-20%Supports: Not neededLayer Height: 0.12Print time: less than 1 day

What you get will be digital files, it is not a physical product. 
  - In the package：Total 13 external spur gears(pinions): m1z9, m1z12, m1z15, m1z18, m1z21, m1z24, m1z27, m1z30, m1z33, m1z36, m1z39, m1z42, m1z45;
Total 10 internal and external spur gears: m1z33z44, m1z42z50,  m1z54z64, m1z63z73, m1z72z82, m1z75z85, m1z81z92, m1z84z95, m1z90z101, m1z93z104

  - Explanationm1z9 – that means the gear’s normal module is 1 and the number of tooth is 9.m1z33z44 – the normal module is 1, quantity of internal teeth is 33 and number of external teeth is 44.

  - Size of gearIf you don’t have professional knowledge about gears, you can calculate the gear’s diameter simply:Diameter≈m*z+(0.5~5)mm.For example, the diameter of gear m1z45 is appr.: 1*45+2=47mm; diameter of m1z33z44 is appr.: 1*44+2=46mmIn this way, you can get the rough size of the gear, but it is not accurate enough for engineering.

You use the parts to assemble at least 10 sets of epicyclic gears that include 3 planetary gears. Any two or more gears can be assembled as transmission train. STEP and DXF format files are included. STEP format files can be used on 3d printer; DXF files is for laser cutting or CNC machining.The parts can be an educational toys for your children too. 
One free epicyclic gear set of them can be downloaded here(m1z9z15z33z44): https://www.twothreed.com/download/epicyclic-gear-set-m1z9z15z33z44/
More about epicyclic gear set: https://www.tanerxun.com/planetary-gear-system/.html
